title: F: outer-shell electrons
hook: Count electrons from the center out.

doesNotKnow: How ground-state electrons are distributed in the first three shells.

misconception: Every electron in an atom is in the outermost occupied shell.
objective: Count outer-shell electrons for a neutral atom among the first 18 elements.

claims.text: A neutral fluorine atom has atomic number 9. In this simplified ground-state shell count, how many electrons are in its outermost occupied shell? A neutral atom has 9 electrons. Its shell count is 2, 7, so its outermost occupied shell has 7.
The rings are a simplified electron-counting model; they do not represent actual electron paths.
Recall: How many total electrons does a neutral fluorine atom have? A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons; its atomic number is 9.
The highlighted outer electrons are a count in the highest occupied shell, not a picture of electrons following circular paths.

recall.question: How many total electrons does a neutral fluorine atom have?
recall.why: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons; its atomic number is 9.
